latest.title: Weekend Showcase Challenge: Timothy, a Personal AI Productivity Agent
latest.description: Timothy is a self-hosted personal AI productivity agent powered by Amazon Bedrock and several other LLM providers. It is designed to help with real tasks instead of only generating text. It can research topics using web search and web fetching, run long-running code sessions, keep long-term memory, run tools in a controlled workspace, and track the cost of model usage.

latest.title: Weekend Showcase Challenge: Serverless Synchronized Countdown Timer
latest.description: Time is relative, especially in web development. If you rely purely on a user's local system clock for a critical web event—like a product drop, a flash sale, or a timed exam—you are trusting a client machine that might be out of sync, manually altered, or drifting due to hardware quirks.

latest.title: We Already Have AI Coding Agents: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot… So Why Kiro?
latest.description: AI coding agents can write and plan code. But can they understand what we're building? Explore Kiro, spec-driven development, and the future of AI-assisted software development.

latest.title: Keeping Serverless Applications and Relational Databases Healthy with Amazon RDS Proxy
latest.description:
Serverless applications make it easy to scale compute capacity.
But there is an important question that often appears when a serverless application connects to a relational database:
What happens when the application scales faster than the database can handle connections?

latest.title: Weekend Showcase Challenge: CJP – Civic Journey Platform | Building Persistent Civic Memory with Amazon Bedrock
latest.description: An agentic civic intelligence platform that transforms citizen reports into persistent, trackable civic issues using Amazon Bedrock, semantic search, and AI-powered accountability workflows. Learn how I built CJP and the lessons I gained while exploring agentic AI applications on AWS.

latest.title: AWS for Beginners: What is Cloud Computing and Why Do We Need AWS?
latest.description: This article is a beginner-friendly introduction to Amazon Web Services (AWS) for freshers with little or no cloud knowledge. It explains what cloud computing is, what AWS offers, why developers use it, and introduces a few important AWS services such as EC2, S3, RDS, and IAM in simple terms.

latest.title: AWS Skill Builder: Building Practical Cloud Skills for the Future
latest.description:
AWS Skill Builder – Empowering Cloud Learning and Career Growth

AWS Skill Builder is a digital learning platform designed to help learners build practical skills in cloud computing and Amazon Web Services (AWS). It provides structured learning resources, interactive content, hands-on experiences, and certification preparation across various AWS technologies. By combining theoretical knowledge with practical learning, AWS Skill Builder enables students and professionals to strengthen their cloud.

latest.title: Integrating Amazon SES SMTP with a Django Application
latest.description: Learn how to integrate Amazon SES SMTP with a Django application to build a flexible and configurable email system. This article covers SMTP configuration, SES credentials, TLS/SSL setup, connection testing, sending limits, and managing multiple email providers directly from a Django CRM.

latest.title: Weekend Showcase Challenge: The Sunday Cross-Word Gazette (1884)
latest.description: What if your everyday minor annoyances could turn into front-page news? The Sunday Cross-Word Gazette transforms modern predicaments into an 1884 Victorian-Desi satirical broadsheet newspaper with an interactive, dynamic crossword puzzle.

latest.title: Weekend Showcase Challenge: RakthaMitra
latest.description: RakthaMitra is a community-focused web application built to organize voluntary blood donor information and make donor discovery simpler.
